title: Working with VBScript Objects
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of working with vbscript objects in a Classic ASP application.
Identify and describe at least two syllabus subtopics: Object variables and The Set statement.
Inspect a minimal example and define a reproducible normal-case and failure-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study working with vbscript objects as part of Classic ASP development and legacy maintenance. The lesson follows the attached ASP curriculum topic 28 and uses the syllabus subtopics as the coverage checklist.
content.why_it_matters: Working with VBScript Objects matters because Classic ASP behavior crosses a server-side scripting engine, IIS configuration, request/response boundaries, and often COM or ADO dependencies. A small, explicit test helps distinguish intended behavior from runtime-specific behavior.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: VBScript is the scripting language used by many Classic ASP applications. In 'Working with VBScript Objects', make input types, empty/null values, scope, and evaluation order explicit: Variant values can change behavior based on the value they contain, and a value read from Request is still untrusted text until validated. Use Option Explicit and small, testable procedures to make mistakes easier to detect.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus coverage
content_blocks.text: The lesson explicitly covers: Object variables; The Set statement; Creating objects with CreateObject; Object properties and methods; Releasing object references; Understanding COM-based objects. Treat these subtopics as connected requirements. For each one, be able to define the concept, identify where it appears in a Classic ASP application, and name one test or diagnostic that would verify it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Working with VBScript Objects
content_blocks.code:
<%
Dim dictionary
Set dictionary = Server.CreateObject("Scripting.Dictionary")
dictionary.Add "status", "ready"
Response.Write Server.HTMLEncode(dictionary("status"))
Set dictionary = Nothing
%>
content_blocks.run_instructions: COM availability and permissions depend on the server. Release object references and avoid placing secret/user-specific mutable data in a shared Application object. The standard CodeLeaf browser playground previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only; it does not execute Classic ASP, VBScript, ADO, IIS commands, PowerShell, or SQL. This block is therefore marked for static inspection unless you run it in the clearly identified local tool.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original sample and test data. Change one condition, input, provider setting, or runtime option at a time, then compare observed behavior with the expected result.
content_blocks.limitations: Not executed during course generation. Classic ASP examples require a configured Windows/IIS environment with the matching ASP scripting engine and any required COM/ADO providers. Provider-specific and IIS-version-specific behavior must be verified locally.

content_blocks.title: Runtime and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Use a local Classic ASP page. Change one value or statement at a time, capture the observed output, and check at least one empty, malformed, or boundary value. The source syllabus treats Classic ASP as a legacy maintenance technology, not as ASP.NET or a default choice for new web projects.

content_blocks.title: Guided workflow
content_blocks.text: 1. Start with a minimal local example of working with vbscript objects. 2. Trace its inputs, state changes, dependencies, and output. 3. Test a normal case, a missing/malformed case, and one permission/provider/runtime failure. 4. Write down the exact expected and observed result before changing another variable.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small, reviewable demonstration of working with vbscript objects using synthetic data. Include at least one of these syllabus concepts: Object variables. State the expected result first, then add one invalid or boundary case and explain how your program should behave.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating legacy runtime behavior as universal.
common_mistakes.why: IIS versions, Windows lifecycle, COM registration/bitness, and ADO providers can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down the actual server/provider versions and validate on a disposable test site.

common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing records, expired sessions, permissions, timeouts, and malformed data reveal different failure modes.
common_mistakes.fix: Add normal, negative, and boundary cases with expected outcomes.

common_mistakes.why: Detailed errors can reveal paths, SQL text, configuration, and component information.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep diagnostics in restricted server-side logs and return a generic message with a reference ID.

task: Build a short demonstration of working with vbscript objects using synthetic data. Demonstrate “Object variables”, state the expected result, and document one edge/failure case.
task_acceptance_criteria: Expected result is written before verification.
At least one invalid or boundary case is documented.
Runtime/provider/version assumptions and security limits are recorded.
hints: Start with the smallest example for object variables.
Keep the sample synthetic and change one thing at a time.
Compare observed behavior against a written expectation and consult the linked official reference if the runtime differs.
summary: Working with VBScript Objects is one step in the larger Classic ASP request, state, data, security, or maintenance workflow.
The syllabus coverage includes Object variables; The Set statement; Creating objects with CreateObject; Object properties and methods; Releasing object references; Understanding COM-based objects.
A reproducible legacy-code example records input, environment/version, expected outcome, observed outcome, and a meaningful failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming syntax alone proves the application works.
common_mistakes.why: IIS configuration, permissions, COM activation, database providers, and response behavior are external dependencies.
common_mistakes.fix: Run against the documented local test host and record exact evidence.

common_mistakes.why: Query strings, form fields, cookies, and hidden controls remain client-controlled.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate on the server and apply authorization and output encoding at the appropriate boundary.
